Package com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec

Interface PrimitiveFloatCodec

  • All Superinterfaces:
    TypeCodec<Float>
    public interface PrimitiveFloatCodec
extends TypeCodec<Float>
    A specialized float codec that knows how to deal with primitive types.

    If the codec registry returns an instance of this type, the driver's float getters will use it to avoid boxing.

      • encode

        @Nullable
default ByteBuffer encode​(@Nullable
                          Float value,
                          @NonNull
                          ProtocolVersion protocolVersion)
        Description copied from interface: TypeCodec
        Encodes the given value in the binary format of the CQL type handled by this codec.
        • Null values should be gracefully handled and no exception should be raised; they should be considered as the equivalent of a NULL CQL value;
        • Codecs for CQL collection types should not permit null elements;
        • Codecs for CQL collection types should treat a null input as the equivalent of an empty collection.
        Specified by:
        encode in interface TypeCodec<Float>

      • decode

        @Nullable
default Float decode​(@Nullable
                     ByteBuffer bytes,
                     @NonNull
                     ProtocolVersion protocolVersion)
        Description copied from interface: TypeCodec
        Decodes a value from the binary format of the CQL type handled by this codec.
        • Null or empty buffers should be gracefully handled and no exception should be raised; they should be considered as the equivalent of a NULL CQL value and, in most cases, should map to null or a default value for the corresponding Java type, if applicable;
        • Codecs for CQL collection types should clearly document whether they return immutable collections or not (note that the driver's default collection codecs return mutable collections);
        • Codecs for CQL collection types should avoid returning null; they should return empty collections instead (the driver's default collection codecs all comply with this rule);
        • The provided ByteBuffer should never be consumed by read operations that modify its current position; if necessary, ByteBuffer.duplicate() duplicate} it before consuming.
        Specified by:
        decode in interface TypeCodec<Float>
